key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier neural operator reconstructs unsteady 3D floating-wind-turbine wakes from two observation planes and transfers across turbine scales with limited retraining.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support downstream-inflow assessment in floating wind farms using sparse wake measurements.
method: Generate fixed and coupled surge–pitch wakes using large-eddy simulation with an actuator line model.
Combine four-dimensional spectral convolutions with continuity and rotor-forced momentum-residual regularization.
Transfer the model from a 5 MW turbine to a 22 MW turbine.
evidence_signal: In simulation-based evaluation, 10% planar sampling nearly matched dense-sampling accuracy (relative L2 error 0.0689 versus 0.0684), while transfer learning reduced 22 MW streamwise-velocity error by 36% versus zero-shot inference at St=0.6.
watch_item: Fine-scale vortex breakdown remains damped, and performance on real-world measurements is not established by the reported simulation tests.
paper_title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
